extracted.intended_audience: issuers of securities, corporate counsel, investor relations and communications teams involved in registered offerings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing public communications and press releases while a registration statement for a securities offering is pending with the SEC, ensuring communications do not constitute an improper 'offer' or trigger gun-jumping. Covers timing, permitted content, and the broad legal scope of what may be treated as an offer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'quiet period'
rubrics_metrics.description: The federal securities laws do not define the term 'quiet period.' The term is used to refer to the period of time surrounding the filing of a registration statement during which an issuer must ensure that its offering-related communications comply with the federal securities laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat 'quiet period' as the regulatory window tied to a pending registration statement; even though not statutorily defined, communications during this time can be restricted. Use caution when labeling communications as outside the offering context because courts and the SEC take a broad view of what counts as an 'offer.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing/duration of the quiet period
rubrics_metrics.description: This period lasts, at a minimum, from the time an issuer files a registration statement with the SEC to the time that SEC staff declare the registration statement 'effective.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume the quiet period is in effect starting at filing and ending only when the registration statement is declared effective. Do not rely on informal or earlier end dates; confirm effectiveness before resuming offering-related communications that would otherwise be restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that offering-related communications comply with federal securities laws
rubrics_metrics.description: During the quiet period issuers and other participants in the registered offering must ensure that any 'offer' of the registered securities is made in accordance with the federal securities laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before issuing press releases or other public statements, evaluate whether the content could be construed as an 'offer' or as promoting investor interest in the securities. Coordinate with legal counsel to confirm compliance with securities statutes and SEC rules to avoid regulatory exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gun-jumping prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: The failure to comply with applicable restrictions on making 'offers' during the quiet period is referred to as 'gun-jumping.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that noncompliance can lead to enforcement consequences. Avoid communications that could be viewed as solicitations or promotional materials for the pending offering until the registration is effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad construction of 'offer' and wide scope of restricted communications
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC and courts have broadly construed the term 'offer' to include communications that might generate public interest in an issuer or its securities, so the scope of communications potentially subject to restriction is quite broad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume only explicit solicitations are restricted; seemingly neutral or informational communications that generate market interest can be problematic. Review communications for any content that could plausibly stimulate investor interest or market demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted communications — factual business information
rubrics_metrics.description: SEC rules permit issuers to communicate during the quiet period about matters other than the registered securities offering, including the release of factual business information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factual, non-promotional business updates may be permissible, but they should be carefully drafted to avoid language that could be interpreted as promoting the offering. Maintain objective tone and avoid forward-looking, promotional, or offering-specific framing without legal clearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted communications — limited disclosure about plans or offering status
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC has rules that permit issuers to provide limited public information about their plans to engage in, or the status of, a registered securities offering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When disclosing limited information about plans or offering status, keep statements narrow, factual, and non-promotional. Coordinate with counsel to ensure disclosures fall within safe-harbor rules and do not inadvertently create an impermissible 'offer.'
